verdict.rationale: Superset documents an authentication layer for its API/MCP surface—OAuth 2.1 + PKCE with dynamic client registration, or API keys, and the hosted MCP server enforces Bearer-token auth via a protected-resource flow—but nothing in the evidence describes actual scope/permission granularity (e.g. read-only vs. write, per-workspace or per-project limits) for these credentials. Missing for 10: documented scopes/permission levels for API keys or OAuth tokens, examples of issuing a restricted-privilege credential, and independent confirmation that least-privilege enforcement actually works.
